**Group:** Diatoms  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

Cells are small, drum- to cylinder-shaped centric diatoms joined into straight chains. Adjacent cells are connected by a ring of long strutted processes around the valve margin, leaving a characteristic open, ladder-like gap between neighbouring cells. This feature can be challenging to see in the planktivoire. Key features: chains of small cylinders, marginal ring of linking tubes, visible inter-cell gap, Two Chloroplasts per cell. Highly abundant.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **thalassiosira** | Thalassiosira cells hang from a single fine central thread and sit close together; Skeletonema cells are bridged by a ring of marginal tubes with an obvious gap. |
| **chaetoceros** | Chaetoceros links cells with thin setae, can be challening to see in Planktovoire. |
